clues.title: Location: island between Britain and Ireland
text: Isle of Man is a British Crown dependency, situated between the United Kingdom and Ireland. So for country streaks purposes, it is counted as the **United Kingdom**.
clues.summary: A British Crown dependency between Britain and Ireland. For country streaks it counts as the United Kingdom.

differs.how: red strip on plates, Gen 2 camera

clues.title: Google car: Gen 2 camera only
text: Coverage on the Isle of Man is limited to **Generation 2**.
This camera can be recognized by the lower camera quality and circular blur above and below. Colours will also seem slightly off.
clues.summary: All coverage is the older Gen 2 camera: lower quality, a round blur above and below, and slightly off colours.

clues.title: Plate: UK style with red strip
text: Similar to the United Kingdom, the Isle of Man uses white front licence plates with yellow rears, but with a **red strip** on the left.

images.caption: Isle of Man plates: white front and yellow rear

clues.summary: White front and yellow rear plates like the UK, but with a red strip on the left. A red strip means Isle of Man.

differs.how: UK plates have no red strip

clues.title: Landscape: hilly farmland, narrow roads
text: The general landscape on the Isle of Man consists of **hilly farmland**, and narrow roads passing through them.

images.caption: A narrow road across open brown moorland with green hills behind

clues.summary: Hilly farmland with narrow roads running through it.

clues.title: Houses: whitewashed walls and entrance walls
text: Houses with **whitewashed walls** and **entrance walls** are a common sight, similar to Ireland.
clues.summary: Whitewashed houses and walls around the entrance are common, a look similar to Ireland.

clues.title: Kerb: striped
text: **Striped kerbs** can sometimes be seen along main roads.
clues.summary: Striped kerbs can sometimes be seen along main roads.

clues.title: Bollard: blue
text: These **blue bollards** can commonly be found in urban areas.
clues.summary: Blue bollards are common in towns and built-up areas.

clues.title: Plants: gorse with yellow flowers
text: [Gorse plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulex) (or Ulex), which can be recognized by their bright **yellow flowers**, are very common on the Isle of Man.
NOTE: Gorse plants can also be found in other rugged areas of the UK and Ireland, such as the Scottish Highlands.
clues.summary: Gorse, a bush with bright yellow flowers, is very common. It also grows in rugged parts of the UK and Ireland, like the Scottish Highlands.

clues.title: Landscape: mostly hilly
text: Isle of Man is generally **quite hilly**, with a few exceptions.
clues.summary: The island is mostly hilly, with a few exceptions.

clues.title: Landscape: flat north, mountains to south
text: Northern Isle of Man is **very flat** in comparison to the rest of the island. Usually, there are mountains visible to the south.
clues.summary: In the north the land is very flat compared to the rest, and mountains are usually visible to the south.

clues.title: Google car: twig smudge on left of lens
text: A** ‘twig smudge’** can be seen on the left side of the camera lens in southern Isle of Man.

images.caption: A dark twig smudge on the left of the Google car lens, circled in the sky

clues.summary: A smudge that looks like a twig sits on the left side of the camera view in the south.

clues.title: Houses: rows of terraced houses
text: Douglas, the capital and **largest town** on the Isle of Man, can be recognized by the rows of **terraced houses**, with a higher population density.
clues.summary: The largest town is recognised by rows of terraced houses and denser buildings. This is the capital, Douglas.

clues.title: Location: town in a NW-SE valley
text: Laxey is a town located in a **northwest-southeast valley**.
clues.summary: The town of Laxey sits in a valley that runs north-west to south-east.

clues.title: Lamp post: blue base, small blue sticker
text: This generic lamp design with a **blue base** and a **small blue sticker** can be found on most of the island, except for around Douglas, and some parts northeast and south. In addition, the top 2 letters can be used to narrow your location down to 1 of the 21 [parishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Local_government_in_the_Isle_of_Man#/media/File:IsleOfMan_LocAuths_and_Sheadings2020.svg).

images.caption: Blue lamp post base with a small blue sticker, highlighted in a red circle at upper left

clues.summary: Lamp posts with a blue base and a small blue sticker cover most of the island, except around Douglas and parts of the northeast and south. The first two letters on the sticker give one of 21 parishes.

clues.title: Lamp post: all green
text: **All green lamps** are commonly found in Ramsey and Castletown, as well as more rarely in the Malew, Santon, and Garff parishes.
clues.summary: All-green lamp posts are common in Ramsey and Castletown, and rarer in the Malew, Santon and Garff parishes.

clues.title: Lamp post: white sticker, two green numbers
text: A small **white sticker** **with 2 green numbers** will be present on lamps in Douglas.

images.caption: A lamp post with a white sticker showing two green numbers; the circle zooms in on it

clues.summary: A small white sticker with two green numbers on lamp posts means Douglas.

clues.title: Lamp post: small yellow sticker
text: A **small yellow sticker** is present on lamps in southern Onchan. The 2 letters are the initials of the road name. E.g. ‘SD’ for Sunningdale Drive.

images.caption: Small yellow sticker on a lamp post, highlighted by a red circle at left

clues.summary: A small yellow sticker with two letters is used in southern Onchan. The letters are the road's initials, like SD for Sunningdale Drive.

clues.title: Sign: oval coat of arms on street signs
text: Many street signs in Ramsey feature the** oval shaped coat of arms**.
clues.summary: Many street signs in Ramsey carry an oval coat of arms.

clues.title: Sign: coat of arms above the text
text: The** coat of arms** is placed** above the text** on many signs in Port Erin.
clues.summary: Many street signs in Port Erin have the coat of arms placed above the street name.

clues.title: Landmark: airport with big flat field
text: The **Ronaldsway Airport** can be recognized by the large, flat and open field with a boundary fence.
clues.summary: Ronaldsway Airport is a large, flat, open field with a boundary fence.

clues.title: Landmark: castle on a small island
text: **The Peel castle**, sitting atop an island, can unsurprisingly, be seen in Peel.
clues.summary: Peel Castle sits on a small island and can be seen from the town of Peel.
